🚨 The truth behind Bruno Guimarães's move to Arsenal: how a beloved captain became "the enemy"
After four and a half years as a hugely popular figure at Newcastle, Bruno Guimarães returned to St James' Park as an opponent. The Telegraph reveals the story behind his £75M move to Arsenal in August and where he stands at his new club.

🎭 From "fury at Isak" to deciding to leave
Guimarães's pride was hurt in summer 2024 when his £100M release clause was not triggered. He was later made captain and shed tears after winning the Carabao Cup in March 2025. Last summer he was furious when Isak announced he wanted to join Liverpool, yet a year later he chose the same path. Turning 28 with his peak years limited, and feeling the club's project had hit a ceiling after Tonali and Gordon were sold, he left it to his agents to engineer his exit without getting his own hands dirty.

🇧🇷 Criticism in Brazil and Howe's departure
This summer's World Cup sealed his decision. He already felt Brazilian media undervalued him because he played for Newcastle, and after missing a penalty against Norway he took the blame for the early exit. That made him determined to test himself at a big club. Once Eddie Howe realised his captain's departure was unavoidable, he resigned, removing the last chance of Guimarães changing his mind.

💰 The mysterious "£45M offer" and the £75M deal
In July, a written "£45M offer" carrying the Arsenal logo was passed to Newcastle through an intermediary, but Arsenal stayed silent for weeks when Newcastle asked for confirmation. The document is believed to have been used to calm Guimarães, who was angry at the lack of progress, and to build pressure for a sale through the media. Direct talks between the clubs began at the end of July, and the move went through after Newcastle issued an ultimatum in early August: £75M in one payment, with no add-ons.

🔴 Arteta pushed it through as a "ready-made" signing
Some at the top of Arsenal had doubts about a £75M fee given his age of 29, a dip in his physical numbers last season and a serious hamstring injury earlier in the year. But Mikel Arteta led the push, arguing he was "a ready-made player worth at least 15 points a season." Partly due to managing his fitness, he has started only four of ten league games this season, but he has shown his big-moment quality by scoring winners off the bench against Sunderland and Leeds.

【Sky Sports】（@psmithXI）
⚽️ From "exceptional" to "complacent": the "next step" Arteta took from the slump at Newcastle
The 2-2 draw at St James' Park showed two extreme sides of Arsenal. They dominated the first half and led 1-0 at the break, but after Mathias Jaissle's triple substitution lifted the home side, they conceded twice and needed Noni Madueke's equaliser to take a point home.

🎤 Arteta on "two points dropped" and the 96-minute standard
After the game Mikel Arteta said: "My feeling is that we dropped two points today. The first half was exceptional at every level, but we didn't make it 2-0, 3-0 or even 4-0." On the start of the second half he admitted: "When the opponent reacted, we were well below the standard required. We gave the ball away cheaply from a throw-in, conceded and gave them belief." He added: "Some players were at the top level for 70 minutes, but at this level that's not enough. Unless you score three or four and can ease off for 15 or 20 minutes, you have to compete for 96 minutes. That is the next step this team has to take."

👀 Redknapp and Wright on the "slack midfield"
The pundits were also critical of the second-half drop. Jamie Redknapp said: "Arsenal were just complacent in the second half. In the first half Declan Rice and Bruno Guimarães had plenty of time, but once Jacob Ramsey came on they were closed down quickly, and Newcastle beat them on second balls and the basics of winning duels." Ian Wright said: "What worries me is the spell where they couldn't get control of the game back. I was really concerned by the Declan Rice and Bruno Guimarães midfield. In that period they didn't look able to push the opponent back."

🔴 Madueke admits the "slack" and the champions' resilience
Noni Madueke, who equalised after Arsenal fell 2-1 behind, praised the team's "mental strength" but admitted about the start of the second half: "We didn't stick to our principles. Because the first half went well, maybe we went into the second half a bit too relaxed." Manchester City also dropped points on the same day, so Arsenal stay top, but together with David Raya's injury, the draw leaves the defending champions with work to do in their bid to retain the title.

【The Athletic】（@ChrisDHWaugh / @gunnerblog / @jacklang）

🔴 Newcastle 2-2 Arsenal

In the first half Arsenal showed all the strength of a team sitting top of the table. They pinned the opposition back, and Eberechi Eze opened the scoring from a superb pass by Kai Havertz. Newcastle were given almost no chances to attack, and Arsenal were steadily moving towards victory.

But everything changed from the start of the second half. A mistake by Martin Ødegaard led to the equaliser, and Arsenal then fell behind from a corner. Noni Madueke levelled in the 78th minute to secure a point, but they missed the chance to stretch the gap to eight points.

It was a game in which the defensive solidity that has underpinned Arsenal's season was shaken.

■ The value Havertz showed

The move that created Eze's opener captured Havertz's excellent decision-making.

After winning the ball from Lewis Hall, he played an exquisite reverse pass in behind the defence. It was a sharp, unexpected assist reminiscent of Mesut Özil.

He was also involved in Madueke's equaliser with a clever flick.

With debate over whether he should be given a new contract, it showed why Mikel Arteta values his intelligence, movement and work rate so highly. He delivered the decisive work demanded of him at the key moments.

■ A defence that crumbled in 45 minutes

Perhaps the dominance of the first half actually bred complacency.

Conceding the equaliser from Ødegaard's poor clearance gave momentum to a Newcastle side that had been passive until then.

For the go-ahead goal from a corner, they left Dan Burn, the tallest player on the pitch, free. They also failed to deal with the scramble in front of goal, and Malick Thiaw forced it in.

What has underpinned Arsenal's strength in the league this season has been an impeccable defence. In the second half here, they fell well below that standard.

■ The substitutions that changed Newcastle

Newcastle were booed at half-time. But head coach Matthias Jaissle made three changes at the break and turned things around.

Jacob Ramsey in particular brought experience and composure to midfield, and the team began pressing higher and more aggressively.

The attacking intensity that had been almost absent in the first half returned, and the whole stadium responded to the momentum.

■ The impact on the title race

Arsenal stay top, provisionally six points clear of Brighton. A draw is by no means a fatal result.

However, it showed that even a team that has been so dominant and consistent can have spells where it falls apart.

On top of that, David Raya came off injured. According to Arteta, he will have an MRI scan the following day, and the extent of the injury is not yet known.

As well as dropping two points, the defensive lapses and the condition of their No 1 remain concerns heading into the next game.https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7792068/2026/11/21/newcastle-2-arsenal-2-premier-league-result/

⚽️ Noni Madueke's equaliser earns Arsenal a point. Second-half turnaround and a mixed homecoming at Newcastle

Leaders Arsenal drew 2-2 with Newcastle at St James' Park. Their run of five straight league wins came to an end, but they provisionally extended their lead over second-placed Brighton to six points.

🔴 First-half control and Eze's opener
Having conceded only five goals in their previous 10 games, Arsenal pressed high from the start and forced distribution errors from Newcastle goalkeeper Lukáš Horníček. In the 33rd minute, Kai Havertz won the ball from Lewis Hall and played a superb pass, and Eberechi Eze ran in behind Amar Dedić to finish calmly. Noni Madueke also had a string of chances to add a second but could not take them, and Newcastle were booed off at half-time.

⚡ A dark start to the second half and Raya's injury
When head coach Matthias Jaissle made a triple substitution at the start of the second half, the home side's momentum changed completely. In the 49th minute, Joe Willock dispossessed Martin Ødegaard, and Harvey Barnes equalised from William Osula's set-up. It was Newcastle's first home goal since 19 September, ending a 312-minute wait. Then in the 62nd minute, after Dan Burn's header from a corner, Malick Thiaw forced the ball home from the scramble to put Newcastle ahead. Shortly afterwards, David Raya was forced off with a shoulder injury, and in the 70th minute former Newcastle captain Bruno Guimarães, booed on every touch, was also substituted.

🎯 The valuable draw Madueke delivered
Arsenal were being pushed back, but in the 78th minute, from a fluid attack, Madueke cut onto his left foot and shot, the ball beating goalkeeper Horníček's hand for the equaliser. Both sides then had chances to win it, but the score did not change. After the match, when Guimarães, who helped deliver the club's first trophy in 56 years with the 2025 Carabao Cup, walked around the pitch, he received cheers from the stands.https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/arsenal-newcastle-goals-premier-league-result-madueke-b3089258.html

【The Guardian】
⚽️ Raya forced off injured but Madueke rescues a point. Arsenal held 2-2 away as new-look Newcastle fight back
For Mikel Arteta, St James' Park remained a tricky place even after Eddie Howe's departure. Leaders Arsenal drew 2-2 with Newcastle to go six points clear of Brighton and Manchester City, but losing David Raya to a left shoulder injury in the second half left the manager looking grim.

🔴 An opener of "efficiency and artistry" in a dominant first half
Before the game, Newcastle had spent around £275M this summer but were struggling to fill the gap left by losing three key players, Bruno Guimarães, Sandro Tonali and Anthony Gordon, and head coach Matthias Jaissle left many of his expensive new signings out of the starting line-up. In the first half Arsenal's high press worked, with Declan Rice and Martin Ødegaard controlling midfield. In the 33rd minute, Kai Havertz won the ball from Lewis Hall and played a superb pass, and Eberechi Eze arrived to strike a beautiful first-time opener.

⚡ Jaissle's triple change, a dark second half and Raya's injury
At half-time the home fans' frustration was close to boiling over, but when Jaissle brought on Tino Livramento, Jacob Ramsey and Anthony Elanga, players who had been at the club since last season, at the start of the second half, the flow changed completely. In the 49th minute, after a rare loss of possession by Ødegaard, Harvey Barnes equalised via William Osula. Then in the 62nd minute, Malick Thiaw forced in Dan Burn's header from a corner to put Newcastle ahead. Straight afterwards, Raya, who had hurt his left shoulder in a collision with Osula, was forced off in visible pain and replaced by Kepa Arrizabalaga.

🎯 Boos from his old club and Madueke's equaliser
Guimarães, who had said last week that he was "loved by the Newcastle fans", was booed as fiercely as a Sunderland player at his old home before being substituted. Even so, in the 78th minute Noni Madueke received Ødegaard's pass on the counter, feinted past two defenders and shot, and the slightly deflected ball slipped through goalkeeper Lukáš Horníček's hands for the equaliser. Arsenal kept top spot, but it was a game that left concerns over the condition of their No 1.https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/21/newcastle-arsenal-premier-league-match-report
